narrative.overview: YTPI's interface makes a household download queue feel familiar and manageable rather than technical. Plain labels, visible progress, responsive navigation, and role-based states help people queue and manage local media.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar Roboto typography and straightforward interface language.
Blue-led palette with light and dark theme roles.
Rounded surfaces, pill-shaped actions, and restrained elevation.
Progress and status stay visible in the download workflow.
Responsive navigation and layouts for desktop and mobile.

rules.name: The Status-Has-a-Color Rule
rules.body: Keep semantic success, warning, error, and in-progress colors attached to the corresponding job state; do not use them as unrelated decoration.

rules.name: The Plain-Language Rule
rules.body: Prefer short, task-oriented labels and explanatory copy; reserve technical monospace text for the detailed output view.

dos: Do preserve the light and dark theme role relationships when extending the UI.
Do keep download status, progress, and percentage together in the job row.
Do use the established blue for primary actions, selection, focus, and progress.
Do keep touch controls at least 44px high where established and preserve visible keyboard focus.
Do let desktop and mobile navigation follow their distinct existing patterns.
donts: Don't use status color as the only indication of a job's state.
Don't make technical output the default content shown to a non-technical user; keep it in details.
Don't remove the configured mobile bottom navigation or ignore its safe-area spacing.
Don't add new palette roles or typefaces without a product or interface need.
